title: 11.1 End-to-end test standalone mode
design:
E2E standalone test scenarios (file: stdr_standalone/test/test_standalone_e2e.cpp)

Suite: StandaloneE2E

Scenarios beyond what test_standalone_backend.cpp already covers:

1. LaserRangesShrinkWhenDrivingTowardWall
   - Map: simple_rooms.yaml
   - Robot: test/test_laser_robot.yaml (180 rays, ±π/2, max_range 4.0)
   - Spawn at known free pose facing a wall
   - Command linear_x = 0.3, run with poll_until until pose advances
   - Assert: center ray range at end < center ray range at start (with margin)

2. MultiRobotFromLauncherConfigDriveIndependently
   - Map: maze1.yaml; Robot: stdr_resources/resources/robots/trin_bot.yaml
   - Spawn two instances at (1,2,π) and (3,2,0)
   - Command linear_x=+0.2 to one, -0.2 to other
   - poll_until until both moved >0.02 m
   - Assert: divergent x trajectories, neither pose nor sensor data of robot A is affected by robot B

3. RobotStopsAtWall
   - Map: maze1.yaml (or whichever map has a clearly hittable wall near spawn)
   - Spawn robot near wall, command forward velocity
   - poll_until until backend.collided(name) == true (with reasonable deadline)
   - Assert: collided flag eventually true; pose did not pass through wall

Test wiring:
- Constants STDR_RESOURCES_DIR / STDR_TEST_DIR follow existing test pattern
- Reuse poll_until() pattern from test_sim_view.cpp (10 ms poll, 2 s deadline)

title: 11.2 End-to-end test ROS2 mode
design:
File: stdr_gui_ros/test/test_ros2_e2e.cpp
Suite: Ros2E2E

Mirrors standalone E2E scenarios (Phase 11.1) but drives through Ros2Backend with real StdrServerNode + StdrRobotNode in-process.

Fixture: reuse pattern from test_ros2_backend_integration.cpp
- SetUpTestSuite rclcpp::init / TearDownTestSuite rclcpp::shutdown
- MultiThreadedExecutor with 4 threads, background spinner thread
- Members: server_node_, backend_node_, Ros2Backend backend_, std::vector<StdrRobotNode::SharedPtr> robot_nodes_
- wait_until(predicate, timeout) helper (10-20 ms poll, multi-second deadline)
- load_map_from_yaml(yaml_path): call stdr_server::load_map() and invoke LoadExternalMap service with resulting OccupancyGrid (already-tested in integration test)
- spawn_robot(description, name_hint optional): SpawnRobot action, returns assigned name
- bring_up_robot_node(name): constructs StdrRobotNode with NodeOptions param robot_name, executor_.add_node()

Scenarios:

1. LaserRangesShrinkWhenDrivingTowardWall
   - Load simple_rooms.yaml (20x15 m). Spawn robot at (5.5, 10.0, 0.0) with one laser sensor: 180 rays, ±π/2 FOV, max_range 4.0, frequency 10 Hz.
   - Bring up robot node; wait_until backend.num_robots()>0.
   - Wait_until backend.latest_laser(name, "laser_0").has_value().
   - range_before = scan.ranges[size/2] (center ray).
   - backend.set_cmd_vel(name, {0.3, 0, 0}).
   - poll_until backend.pose(name)->x - spawn.x >= 0.1 (3 s deadline).
   - Drain next scan, sample range_after.
   - EXPECT_LT(range_after, range_before - 0.05).

2. MultiRobotIndependentDrive
   - Load simple_rooms.yaml. Spawn two robots at (3,7,0) and (15,7,π) with minimal sensor configs (laser sufficient).
   - Bring up both robot nodes.
   - wait_until backend.num_robots()==2.
   - backend.set_cmd_vel(name_a, {0.2,0,0}); set_cmd_vel(name_b, {0.2,0,0}).
   - poll_until both pose deltas >= 0.02 (3 s).
   - Assert: pose_a.x > spawn_a.x; pose_b.x < spawn_b.x; |pose.y - spawn.y| < 0.1 for both.

3. (SKIPPED) RobotStopsAtWall — Ros2Backend::collided() is FIXME-CLAUDE stub. Blocked by bead fzz (add collision topic to stdr_robot). Document in test file comment that this scenario lives only in standalone E2E suite until fzz lands.

CMake:
- ament_add_gtest(test_ros2_e2e test/test_ros2_e2e.cpp)
- target_compile_definitions: STDR_RESOURCES_DIR
- target_link_libraries: ${PROJECT_NAME}, stdr_server::stdr_server, stdr_robot::stdr_robot, GTest::gmock
- ament_target_dependencies as needed for stdr_msgs, nav_msgs, rclcpp_action

Notes:
- Heap corruption at exit (bead 642) may affect this binary too; do not block on it — file failure is gtest-pass + colcon return -6 footgun, separate cleanup work.
- Per CLAUDE.md tf2_spin_thread=false; do not start tf2 spin threads.
- Use minimal sensor configs to keep per-tick cost low.

title: Fix laser/sensor noise model: treat noise_mean as zero, not bias
description: LaserSimulator (and likely other sensors) apply noise as a std::normal_distribution with config.noise.mean as the mean, then add the sample directly to the true range. With hokuyo's noise_mean=0.5, every beam gets a +0.5 m bias — visible as beams overextending obstacles in standalone GUI. Fix: center noise at zero (zero-mean Gaussian) so noise_mean acts as documented variance-only config. Audit all sensor simulators for the same pattern.
notes: Draft PR opened: https://github.com/bgill92/stdr_simulator/pull/23 (base: jazzy-devel). Awaiting review before merge.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #23 (merged 2026-04-14). Laser/sonar use zero-mean Gaussian; noise.mean intentionally ignored.

Auto-generate sensor frame_ids when YAML omits them
description:
Robot YAMLs (e.g., pandora_robot.yaml) and external sensor YAMLs
(e.g., laser_sensors/hokuyo/hokuyo_URG_04LX.yaml) do not specify
frame_id. stdr_simulation::config_loader leaves cfg.frame_id empty.

In ROS2 mode, stdr_robot publishes on '<robot_name>/<frame_id>'. With
empty frame_id, this becomes 'robot0/' — trailing slash —
rclcpp::exceptions::InvalidTopicNameError.

Repro: ros2 launch stdr_launchers server_with_map_and_gui_plus_robot.launch.py
Crash: stdr_gui_ros_node terminates with InvalidTopicNameError on
robot0/ when subscribing to laser/sonar topics.

Test test_ros2_backend_integration masks the bug by injecting explicit
frame_ids ("laser0", "sonar0") in its goal, never via YAML. The bug
predates Phase 10 — Phase 6/9 simply never exercised the YAML path
end-to-end.

Fix: auto-generate frame_ids in stdr_simulation::config_loader
post-parse: 'laser_0', 'laser_1', 'sonar_0', etc., for entries with
empty frame_id. Preserve any YAML-supplied values.

Apply to all sensor types: laser, sonar, rfid, co2, thermal, sound.

Blocks Phase 10 manual e2e validation.
close_reason: Fixed in stdr_simulation::load_robot_config — auto-generates positional frame_ids (laser_N, sonar_N, etc.) for sensors with empty frame_id. Stable index preserves slot when mixed with explicit names.

Configurable sim timestep for ROS2 integration (Phase 6/9)
description:
Decouple simulation physics dt from per-sensor publish rates, TF rate, and odom rate. Logic lives in stdr_simulation (shared engine) so standalone and ROS2 share semantics.

Full design: .claude/plans/DECOUPLED_RATES_PLAN.md

Design decisions:
- Scope: both modes via shared engine (single source of truth).
- Rate <-> dt: snap to nearest tick multiple. period_ticks = max(1, round(1 / (freq * dt))). Accumulator strategy deferred (child 8aa.7).
- TF/odom: separate parameters/setters. Defaults TF=50 Hz, odom=10 Hz.
- Sensor freq: from YAML 'frequency' field (already loaded). 0/missing = every tick (backwards-compatible).
- GUI: status display only (no sliders); rates set via config/params.

ROS2 robot parameters:
- sim_step_dt (default 0.1, bounds 0.001-1.0).
- tf_rate (default 50.0, bounds 0.0-1000.0).
- odom_rate (default 10.0, bounds 0.0-1000.0).
- Parameter callback validates bounds, reconciles scheduler, recreates sim_timer_ if needed.

Children (sequenced):
- 8aa.1 RateScheduler in stdr_simulation + tests (Phase A).
- 8aa.2 Engine integration: TF/odom/sensor stream dispatch (Phase B, depends 8aa.1).
- 8aa.3 StandaloneBackend wiring + status (Phase C, depends 8aa.2).
- 8aa.4 StdrRobotNode params + scheduler dispatch (Phase D, depends 8aa.2).
- 8aa.5 Ros2Backend param propagation (Phase E, depends 8aa.4).
- 8aa.6 GUI status panel rows for rates (Phase F, depends 8aa.3 + 8aa.5).
- 8aa.7 Follow-up: sub-tick accumulator strategy (depends 8aa.1).

Open risks (see plan):
- Timer recreate race on sim_step_dt param change (mitigate via mutex or defer).
- TF rate clamp when tf_rate > 1/sim_step_dt.
- Ros2Backend robot discovery mechanism (TBD before Phase E).
close_reason: All 6 phase children (8aa.1-8aa.6) merged. 8aa.7 remains as standalone P3 follow-up.

title: RateScheduler in stdr_simulation + tests (Phase A)
description:
Add RateScheduler component to stdr_simulation. Maps target rates (TF, odom, per-sensor) to integer tick multiples of sim_step_dt.

Files:
- stdr_simulation/include/stdr_simulation/rate_scheduler.hpp (new)
- stdr_simulation/src/rate_scheduler.cpp (new)
- stdr_simulation/test/test_rate_scheduler.cpp (new)

API (see plan for exact signatures):
- set_step_dt(double): recomputes all cached period_ticks.
- set_rate(Stream, index, freq_hz): registers stream. freq<=0 => every tick.
- tick(): advance one step; return events for streams firing this tick.
- effective_rate(Stream, index): returns 1 / (period_ticks * dt).

Snap formula:
- period_ticks = max(1, round(1.0 / (freq * dt))).

Tests:
- freq=0 => every tick.
- freq=10, dt=0.1 => period=1.
- freq=5, dt=0.1 => period=2.
- freq=0.5, dt=0.1 => period=20.
- freq=100, dt=0.1 => period=1 (clamp).
- Changing dt recomputes all periods.
- effective_rate returns 1/(period*dt).

Part of stdr_simulator-8aa. See .claude/plans/DECOUPLED_RATES_PLAN.md Phase A.

title: Engine integration: TF/odom/sensor stream dispatch (Phase B)
description:
Integrate RateScheduler into SimulationEngine. Engine always runs physics every step; scheduler tells engine which streams (TF, odom, per-sensor) fire this tick.

Files:
- stdr_simulation/include/stdr_simulation/simulation_engine.hpp
- stdr_simulation/src/simulation_engine.cpp
- stdr_simulation/test/test_simulation_engine.cpp

Changes:
- Engine holds RateScheduler member.
- set_step_dt forwards to scheduler.
- New: set_tf_rate(double), set_odom_rate(double).
- Per-sensor rates set on robot/config registration with engine.
- step(dt): physics always runs. scheduler.tick() returns events; engine simulates/caches matching sensors.
- Cache latest sensor measurements between firings so consumers can read at any time.

Tests:
- 20 steps at dt=0.1: laser at 5 Hz fires 10x, odom at 10 Hz fires 20x, TF at 50 Hz clamps to 20x.

test_ros2_backend SIGABRT during teardown (pre-existing)
description:
colcon test --packages-select stdr_gui_ros reports test_ros2_backend
exits with non-zero status. All 25 gtest cases pass; the failure is a
SIGABRT during process teardown after tests complete.

Diagnostic: malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected,
suggesting heap corruption in either the StandaloneBackend simulation
loop teardown or the in-process Ros2Backend / StdrRobotNode shutdown.

Test runner attributed it to stdr_standalone teardown interleaving with
stdr_gui_ros via concurrent CTest output; XML result file records
failures="0".

Reproduced on jazzy-devel HEAD (commit 77f0b1f) without the Phase 10
changes applied — predates rmi.

Severity: blocks clean colcon test runs but not test correctness.
notes:
## Root cause (investigated 2026-05-07)

NOT stdr code. Crash is in liblttng-ust's atexit destructor:

```
#26 lttng_ust_exit ()  from .pixi/envs/default/lib/liblttng-ust.so.1
#27 _dl_call_fini
#28 _dl_fini
#29 __run_exit_handlers
```

Path: liblttng-ust dtor → pthread_cancel → lazy dlopen("libgcc_s.so.1") → malloc(4576) → glibc walks fastbin → detects pre-existing corruption → SIGABRT.

Stdr code, Ros2Backend dtor, and SPSC ring buffers are all clear. Repros with a single trivial test (DefaultStepDtIsKDefaultStepDt) that does no ROS2 activity. Only repros under ctest's run_test.py harness (subprocess.Popen with stdout=PIPE), not under direct invocation.

Pulled in transitively: rclcpp → tracetools → liblttng-ust (pixi/robostack-jazzy packaging).

## Recommended fix (option 1)

Force eager load of libgcc_s.so.1 so pthread_cancel doesn't dlopen during atexit:

```cmake
target_link_libraries(test_ros2_backend
  ${PROJECT_NAME} GTest::gmock_main
  -Wl,--no-as-needed gcc_s -Wl,--as-needed)
```

Standard ROS2 atexit-crash workaround.

## Scope

Likely affects ALL ROS2 test binaries in this workspace (any pkg linking rclcpp+gtest). Better to apply via a shared CMake helper than per-test. Worth widening this bead or filing a separate repo-wide tracking bead.

## Related findings

- test_ros2_backend_integration also fails (different cause: RegisterRobot times out / "unknown goal response, ignoring..."). File separate bead.
- CMakeLists.txt has no sanitizer plumbing. Adding STDR_*_ENABLE_ASAN opt-in would speed future diagnosis.

title: Investigate: Custom plotting panel with sim data access + command injection
description:
Epic to investigate adding a user-extensible plotting panel alongside the map view, with safe access to simulation data and the ability to command robots from the plotting thread. Motivation: downstream work on SLAM/navigation algorithms needs live introspection of sim state (poses, scans, odometry, collisions) and the ability to drive robots programmatically while visualizing custom metrics.

Scope of investigation:

1. Plot panel architecture
   - ImPlot integration (already vendored) as dockable panel next to map.
   - Plotter plugin/registry pattern — user writes a C++ Plotter subclass, registers at startup. Decide whether hot-reload via shared libs is stretch goal or out-of-scope.
   - Configurable layout: multiple plots, tabs, or single panel.

2. Thread-safe data transfer (sim -> plot)
   - Compare options:
     a) Double-buffered snapshot per sim tick (simple, latest-only).
     b) SPSC/MPMC ring buffer per metric (history preserved, lock-free).
     c) Mutex-guarded latest snapshot.
   - Recommendation leaning SPSC ring buffer — time-series plots need history.
   - Identify per-robot vs global metrics.

3. Introspection API (extend SimulatorBackend)
   - num_robots(), robot_ids(), sensors_on(robot_id), pose(robot_id), twist, latest_scan(robot, sensor), collision_state, sim_time.
   - Snapshot-consistent reads — no torn state.
   - Same interface implemented by StandaloneBackend (direct SimulationEngine access) and Ros2Backend (topic subscriber cache).

4. Command injection (plot -> sim)
   - MPSC command queue drained by sim thread each tick.
   - Command types: VelocityCommand, TeleportRobot (debug), PauseResume.
   - Reuse same path as keyboard teleop where possible.
   - ROS2 backend publishes to cmd_vel topics.

5. Helper utilities for plotters
   - Iteration helpers (for each robot, for each sensor).
   - Unit conversions, coordinate transforms.
   - Time-aligned sampling helpers.

Open questions:
- Should Plotter plugins be static-registered at compile time, or loaded as shared libs at runtime?
- How do we prevent a slow/buggy plotter from stalling the GUI thread?
- Do we need recording/playback for offline plot development?
- Rate-limit strategy: plot at GUI refresh rate, not sim rate?

Deliverable: design doc outlining recommended architecture, interface sketches, and task breakdown for a follow-up implementation epic.

title: Ros2Backend does not pick up external sim_step_dt/tf_rate/odom_rate changes (one-way sync)
description:
After Phase 8aa.5, Ros2Backend propagates set_step_dt/set_tf_rate/set_odom_rate from the GUI to robot nodes via AsyncParametersClient. But the reverse direction is not wired: when a robot's parameters are changed externally (e.g. via 'ros2 param set /stdr_robot tf_rate 25.0'), the GUI info panel keeps showing the backend's stale cached values.

Repro:
  ros2 launch stdr_launchers server_with_map_and_gui.launch.py
  ros2 run stdr_robot robot_spawner --description <yaml> --x 1 --y 2 --theta 0
  # GUI info panel shows TF: 50.0, Odom: 10.0, Sim step: 0.10
  ros2 param set /stdr_robot sim_step_dt 0.05
  ros2 param set /stdr_robot tf_rate 25.0
  ros2 param set /stdr_robot odom_rate 5.0
  # Robot node actually applies the change (verifiable via 'ros2 param get'),
  # but the GUI panel still displays the old values.

Root cause: Ros2Backend::get_step_dt / get_tf_rate / get_odom_rate return local atomic caches written only by set_*. There is no subscription to /parameter_events and no periodic refresh from get_parameters.

Fix options:
- rclcpp::ParameterEventHandler per discovered robot, on_active_robots-lifecycled, that updates the local atomics when the robot's parameter changes externally.
- On AsyncParametersClient creation (in on_active_robots), do a one-shot get_parameters to seed the cache from the robot's actual defaults (handles the case where the robot was launched with overrides that differ from kDefaultTfRate/kDefaultOdomRate).

Tests:
- Extend test_ros2_backend with a propagation-in-reverse test: spawn mock node with non-default rates, wait for backend cache to converge.

Discovered while verifying 8aa.6.

Sonar max-range sentinel emits range > max_range on no-hit
description: In stdr_simulation/src/sensors/sonar_simulator.cpp around line 76, when the inner ray loop finds no obstacle, min_steps remains max_steps + 1, so the computed range is (max_steps + 1) * map.resolution, which exceeds config.max_range by one cell (e.g., 5.1 m for max_range=5, resolution=0.1). The subsequent clamp at line 88 uses >= config.max_range so it gets flipped to +infinity — the current documented behavior — but the intermediate value is off-by-one. Likely fix: use min_steps = max_steps as the 'no hit' sentinel so the natural no-hit range equals max_range exactly, or restructure to set range to +inf directly on no-hit. title: Launch file name= remap collapses StdrRobotNode and robot_spawner_client into same name
description:
server_with_map_and_gui_plus_robot.launch.py spawns the robot via:

    Node(package='stdr_robot', executable='robot_spawner', name='robot_spawner', ...)

The name='robot_spawner' argument applies the rclcpp remap __node:=robot_spawner to the entire process. The robot_spawner executable creates two nodes:
  1. rclcpp::Node('robot_spawner_client')  -- action client
  2. StdrRobotNode  -- node name hardcoded as 'stdr_robot' inside the class

With the launch-side remap, both nodes try to take the name 'robot_spawner' inside the same context. The second one fails to register cleanly with DDS, so /stdr_robot never appears.

Symptom: after launching server_with_map_and_gui_plus_robot.launch.py, ros2 node list shows /robot_spawner, /stdr_gui, /stdr_server, /world2map but NO /stdr_robot. ros2 param list /stdr_robot fails with 'Node not found'.

Workaround (manual): run the spawner without launch's name= remap:

    ros2 run stdr_robot robot_spawner --description <yaml> --x 1 --y 2 --theta 0

/stdr_robot appears as expected.

Fix candidates:
- Drop name= from the Node action in server_with_map_and_gui_plus_robot.launch.py.
- Apply the remap only to the action-client node (not feasible from launch level), OR
- Change StdrRobotNode to accept its node name from the robot_name parameter at construction (i.e., name the node after the robot, e.g., robot0). That also fixes the longer-term multi-robot DDS rendezvous issue noted in the 8aa.5 PR description.

Repro:
  ros2 launch stdr_launchers server_with_map_and_gui_plus_robot.launch.py
  ros2 node list   # /stdr_robot missing
